sections.heading: Glossary term: Astronaut
sections.body: An astronaut is a person who is qualified to be part of a crew onboard a space flight. Astronauts are trained in the operation of rockets, space stations, and to solve specialized technical problems that are unique to trips outside Earth's atmosphere. They are often trained to carry out science experiments in space. A few astronauts have even walked on the Moon. Astronaut was originally used to refer to space crews from the United States of America but is now a general term used by many different countries. Russian space crew are called cosmonauts, Chinese space crew are often called taikonauts, and European space crew are called spationauts.

sections.source_html:
Glossary term: Astronaut

Also known as cosmonaut, taikonaut or spationaut

Description: An astronaut is a person who is qualified to be part of a crew onboard a space flight. Astronauts are trained in the operation of rockets, space stations, and to solve specialized technical problems that are unique to trips outside Earth's atmosphere. They are often trained to carry out science experiments in space. A few astronauts have even walked on the Moon. Astronaut was originally used to refer to space crews from the United States of America but is now a general term used by many different countries. Russian space crew are called cosmonauts, Chinese space crew are often called taikonauts, and European space crew are called spationauts.

Related Terms:

  • Rocket
  • Space Station
  • Spacecraft


See this term in other languages

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. You can find a full list of credits here. All glossary terms and their definitions are released under a Creative Commons CC BY-4.0 license and should be credited to "IAU OAE".

If you notice a factual error in this glossary definition then please get in touch.
sections.body_ru: Астронавт — человек, подготовленный к работе в составе экипажа космического полёта. Астронавты учатся управлять космическими кораблями и станциями и решать технические задачи, характерные для работы за пределами земной атмосферы. Их часто готовят к проведению научных экспериментов в космосе. Двенадцать участников программы «Аполлон» побывали на поверхности Луны. Словом «астронавт» сначала называли участников американских космических экипажей. Сейчас это слово используют во многих странах. В России принято название «космонавт». Китайских участников космических полётов иногда называют тайконавтами. Во Франции для своих астронавтов также употребляют слово spationaute («спасионавт»). Европейское космическое агентство называет участников своего отряда астронавтами.

Caption: European Space Agency astronaut Alexander Gerst (Germany) during an extravehicular activity (EVA) at the International Space Station (ISS) in 2014. His shift outside the ISS took more than six hours.
Credit: NASA credit link

License: CC-BY-NC-2.0 Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 2.0 Generic icons


Astronauts working outside the ISS

Caption: In this image, astronauts Robert L. Curbeam (USA) and Christer Fuglesang (Sweden) are seen working outside the International Space Station (ISS), visible against the backdrop of the Earth with New Zealand visible below. They are attaching a truss segment to the ISS to keep it rigid and to route electricity and liquid coolants. Extending over 15 meters and weighing more than 10,000 kilograms, these trusses are not easy objects to work with, especially outside of a space station. The astronauts are wearing large white spacesuits and are attached to the hull of the ISS to ensure they do not drift off into space.
Credit: STS-116 Shuttle Crew, NASA credit link

media.caption_en: In this image, astronauts Robert L. Curbeam (USA) and Christer Fuglesang (Sweden) are seen working outside the International Space Station (ISS), visible against the backdrop of the Earth with New Zealand visible below. They are attaching a truss segment to the ISS to keep it rigid and to route electricity and liquid coolants. Extending over 15 meters and weighing more than 10,000 kilograms, these trusses are not easy objects to work with, especially outside of a space station. The astronauts are wearing large white spacesuits and are attached to the hull of the ISS to ensure they do not drift off into space.
media.caption_ru: На этом изображении астронавты Роберт Л. Кёрбим (США) и Кристер Фуглесанг (Швеция) работают за пределами Международной космической станции (МКС) на фоне Земли, внизу видна Новая Зеландия. Они прикрепляют сегмент фермы к МКС, чтобы сохранить её жёсткость и проложить электрические и жидкостные охлаждающие магистрали. Протяжённостью более 15 метров и массой более 10 000 килограммов, эти фермы не являются простыми объектами для работы, особенно за пределами космической станции. Астронавты одеты в большие белые скафандры и прикреплены к корпусу МКС, чтобы не улететь в космос.
